answer: A job board can give each verified human one daily posting credit, even when that human runs many agents. A registrar checks biometric uniqueness, stores an encrypted template in a vault and issues a blind credential. Each post reveals a daily nullifier so a mirror account cannot spend the same credit twice. The nebula of aliases still shares one allowance; extra capacity requires recruiting distinct people. This depends on accurate deduplication and secure enrollment, risks excluding legitimate users and needs a privacy-preserving appeal process.
